deviations.item: Scales are calibrated from the candidate's own encoder and codebooks after the existing 50-epoch warm-up, rather than from a separately executed baseline warm-up checkpoint.
deviations.reason: The frozen tree provides no baseline checkpoint-and-resume handoff for this experiment. Using its first 50 epochs as the short warm-up keeps the same model initialization, optimizer, scheduler, batch size, seeds, and total 3000-epoch schedule while avoiding an external checkpoint dependency. This is an operational interpretation, not a claim that the warm-up is an independent baseline run.

deviations.item: The per-stage statistic is implemented as sqrt(mean over train items and latent coordinates of residual squared), equivalent to sqrt(mean_train(||r||^2)/d); scale calibration enumerates the complete training-item tensor on each rank.
deviations.reason: This directly implements the specified population RMS per coordinate using only train target items. The dataset is small enough for the existing training device path and repeated rank-local calculation avoids introducing a new distributed aggregation mechanism.

deviations.item: Calibration is performed for all three stages, including the first stage, and each stage's quantization loss is computed in normalized residual coordinates.
deviations.reason: The provided formula defines s_l and normalized quantization u_l for every stage, while also describing later-stage tempering. The literal per-stage definition was followed; the existing loss applied to each stage's transformed input/output without adding loss weights.

deviations.item: The complete 3000-epoch run and Stage 3 ranking evaluation were not executed; the smoke test uses a compact synthetic fixture.
deviations.reason: The requested verification is a minimal runability smoke test. A full training and downstream evaluation are materially longer; Stage 3 changes or shared evaluation modifications are outside the owned candidate tree. Production constants retain the frozen 3000-epoch protocol.

assumptions: The unique target IDs in the existing train.parquet define train items for scale estimation, and embedding row indices match item IDs, as in the frozen baseline loader/exporter.
The existing 50-epoch warm-up is the intended 'short baseline warm-up' boundary; scales become active beginning with epoch 51 and remain fixed thereafter, including inference/export.

The baseline optimizer and scheduler continue through warm-up without reset, since the protocol requires preserving the existing optimizer and schedule and does not specify a reset at scale activation.

Use of rank-local full train-item calibration is valid because DDP parameters/codebooks are synchronized by the preceding training and every rank evaluates the same train-item set; no validation/test items contribute.

notes: Standalone copy of stage2_RQ-VAE/TIGER_RQ-VAE, with production inputs and frozen training constants retained. The candidate implements fixed stage scales as a non-trainable buffer in RQLayer: warm-up residual RMS is measured train-only; subsequent inputs are divided by the scale, quantized by the existing nearest-code rule, and quantized contributions are multiplied by the same scale before residual subtraction and reconstruction accumulation. The scales are part of model state and are used during index generation/export. Candidate SID, JSON, checkpoint, and training metrics/log outputs resolve inside this tree. Only this tree and the requested implementation.json were written; no baseline, shared repository code, MCP server, or verification code was modified.
